related_questions.question: What are the four types of COVID vaccines?

text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, there are primarily two types of COVID-19 vaccines currently recommended: mRNA vaccines and protein subunit vaccines. While the viral vector vaccine from Johnson & Johnson was previously used, it is no longer available.
snippet_highlighted_words: mRNA vaccines and protein subunit vaccines

list.title: mRNA Vaccines:
list.snippet: These vaccines, like those from Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, use messenger RNA to instruct cells to produce a harmless piece of the virus (the spike protein) which then triggers an immune response.

list.title: Protein Subunit Vaccines:
list.snippet: The Novavax vaccine is an example of this type. It contains harmless pieces of the virus (proteins) that stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies.

list.title: Viral Vector Vaccines:
list.snippet: While no longer available in the US, the Johnson & Johnson vaccine was a viral vector vaccine. These vaccines use a modified version of a different virus (the vector) to deliver genetic material from the COVID-19 virus to cells, triggering an immune response.
